description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06) by the review probes for s507c PART TWO; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466 and on the batch's
tree alike.  Probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/p2/ar.pl (AR_DIR=<fresh dir> IMPL ar.pl < /dev/null; answers ar.perl /
ar.main / ar.dev), rows 24 and 8.

(1) row 24:   { local ($^I, @ARGV) = ("", "f1"); while (<>) { print ARGVOUT "via $_" } }
      perl: f1 becomes "via a1\nvia a2\n"        PCL: f1 is EMPTY -- the file was truncated for the edit and nothing was
      written, with no message.  A plain `print` (the selected handle) in the same loop is RIGHT, so ARGVOUT as a NAME is
      not bound to the stream the in-place edit selects.  s507c's #2669 touches how the ARGVOUT selection is saved and
      restored for a nested edit; if its agent did not take this half, the mechanism to reuse is whatever makes the
      selected handle answer to that name (rule 11).
      Why it matters although the spelling is rare: it destroys the user's file silently.

(2) row 8:    local @ARGV = ("f1", "f2"); my @all = <>; my $after = <>;
      perl: the second `<>` finds @ARGV empty and reads STDIN (with /dev/null: undef, and `$.` is 0 afterwards); with a
      terminal or a pipe on STDIN it would return its lines.  PCL: undef, `$.` stays 5, STDIN is never consulted.
      Low priority: a program that reads `<>` to the end and then reads `<>` again is unusual.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken) for (1): `print {*ARGVOUT} ...` and `print {select()} ...` in the same loop --
if the second writes and the first does not, the name lookup is the whole bug.
subject: ARGV residue after s507c: (1) DATA LOSS -- in an in-place edit `print ARGVOUT "..."` (the handle named explicitly) writes nothing and the edited file ends up EMPTY; (2) after `<>` has exhausted @ARGV one more `<>` does not start over on STDIN
